title: Cutting Tools
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Pre-Technical Studies; not yet checked by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher; safety lines marked SAFETY in the library to confirm first; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: SAFETY: cutting tools are used only with the teacher present, work held in a vice or clamp. Using the tools (outcome c) is watched and marked with the rubric.

skills.key_step: The learner identifies cutting tools (saws: tenon, cross-cut, rip, hacksaw, coping; chisels; planes; snips; knives; files), selects the tool for a task by the material and the cut, and cares for them (keep sharp, clean, oil steel, guard edges, store in racks); caring for the tools in class is watched and marked with the rubric.

floor.prerequisite: Knows how to care for measuring tools.
floor.question: What do you do to a steel tool after use?

representations: saws laid out with teeth visible
steps: Say how to care for it.

board.do: Write three tasks: cut a steel rod, smooth a board, cut a plank across the grain.
Wait for the learner to say a hacksaw, fine hard teeth.
Choose tools for the other tasks.

misconceptions.repair: Compare the teeth: a tenon saw has bigger teeth for wood; a hacksaw has fine hard teeth for metal.

misconceptions.ask: Which tool smooths a wooden board?
misconceptions.repair: Plane a board to show long smooth shavings; chisel a joint to show cutting out small parts.

misconceptions.ask: Why should a cutting tool be kept sharp?
misconceptions.repair: Explain that a blunt tool needs more force and slips; compare cutting card with sharp and blunt scissors.

misconceptions.ask: Which saw cuts wood across the grain?
misconceptions.repair: Show the grain on a plank; cross-cut goes across it, rip goes along it. Look at the tooth shapes.

checks.question: Why is a cutting tool kept sharp?
checks.answer: It cuts easily and slips less

skills.key_step: The learner explains the safe use of cutting tools: work held in a vice or clamp, cutting away from the body, hacksaw teeth pointing forward, cuts started gently then long steady strokes, tools carried pointing down, blunt or loose tools reported; the use is watched and marked with the rubric. SAFETY: teacher confirms.
representations: a hacksaw blade under a magnifier
steps: Check the tool is sharp and the blade fitted the right way.
Cut away from the body, start gently.
Clean the tool and put it back.
contexts: cutting a metal rod for a shelf bracket
cutting a plank for a stool

board.do: Draw a learner holding a piece of wood in one hand and sawing with the other.

board.say: What is unsafe, and what should be done?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say clamp it in a vice.
Redraw with the work in a vice.

listen_for: Towards the body, for more control
misconceptions.ask: In which direction should a chisel or knife cut?
misconceptions.repair: Show the path the blade takes if it slips in each direction; agree the rule and practise on a clamped scrap.

listen_for: In one hand while the other hand saws
misconceptions.ask: How is a small piece of wood held while it is sawn?
misconceptions.repair: Show how a saw jumps at the start of a cut; clamp the work and saw with the free hand guiding safely.

misconceptions.ask: Which way do the teeth of a hacksaw blade point?
misconceptions.repair: Look at the teeth with a magnifier; fit the blade so they point forward and feel the cut on the push.

listen_for: Press hard with fast short strokes
misconceptions.ask: How should you start a saw cut?
misconceptions.repair: Start a cut with a thumb guiding the blade (above the teeth) and light strokes; then use the full length of the blade.

misconceptions.ask: How is a chisel carried in the workshop?
misconceptions.repair: Show the injury a blade in a pocket can cause in a fall; practise carrying tools pointing down.

checks.question: Which way do hacksaw teeth point?
How is small work held while cutting?
checks.answer: In a vice or with a clamp
